Samsung SDI.why: lithium-ion battery maker whose small cells go into data-center BBUs (battery back-up units) and whose ESS / UPS batteries serve AI data-center power demand; data-center backup power is a growth market it names in its own filing
Samsung SDI.evidence: Small batteries are expanding into micro-mobility and data-center BBUs (Battery Back-up Units); the company expects new applications including BBUs driven by the growth of AI data centers to sustain small-battery growth, and is developing a high-power UPS ESS module for AI loads (Samsung SDI half-year report, DART 08-14-2026)

players.product: lithium-ion cells for data-center BBUs (battery back-up units) and high-power UPS / ESS battery modules for AI loads

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 half-year report (DART, filed 08-14-2026, consolidated): H1 revenue KRW 7,345,161M, up 16% year on year; H1 operating profit KRW 48,194M, an improvement of KRW 8,801 hundred million year on year (H1 2025 operating loss KRW 831,905,582 thousand on revenue KRW 6,356,223,797 thousand). Q2 alone: revenue KRW 3,768,808,123,247 and operating profit KRW 203,774,585,157. Energy Solution (batteries) revenue KRW 6,873,362M (94%) with an operating loss of KRW 17,324M; Electronic Materials revenue KRW 471,799M (6%) with operating profit KRW 65,518M. Other operating income (US IRA advanced manufacturing production tax credit) KRW 188,137M. H1 revenue by region: North America KRW 2,259,222,453 thousand, Europe KRW 2,268,854,978 thousand, Korea KRW 526,271,600 thousand, China KRW 655,021,175 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 revenue KRW 7,345,161M (+16% YoY); H1 OP KRW 48,194M; Q2 revenue KRW 3,768,808,123,247, Q2 OP KRW 203,774,585,157; Energy Solution OP KRW -17,324M

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center role (the company's own description in the report): small batteries are widening their applications to micro-mobility and data-center BBUs (Battery Back-up Units); the company says ESS batteries keep growing strongly on renewables and rising power demand from more AI data centers, expects the ESS market to grow faster on AI data-center power demand, and expects small-battery demand to keep growing on new applications including BBUs for AI data centers, robots and aerospace. It says markets needing high output such as BBUs, professional power tools and hybrid EVs are expanding and it is growing that business on its high-power battery strength. R&D in H1 2026: a high-power UPS ESS module (microcycling UPS module for AI loads) is in development; an earlier high-power UPS ESS module raising discharge power per rack for a 5-minute backup system is completed.

Capacity and utilisation, H1 2026: small batteries (Cheonan, Tianjin etc.) capacity 1,178 million cells, production 860 million, utilisation 73%; EMC (semiconductor encapsulant, Gumi) capacity 2,290 tons, production 648 tons, utilisation 28%. Average selling price of small batteries KRW 2,923 per cell (FY2025: KRW 2,930; FY2024: KRW 3,287). Small-battery market share 12% (TSR basis; FY2025 13%). H1 capex KRW 10,928 (KRW 100 million units) for capacity expansion etc. -- Energy Solution 10,809, Electronic Materials 119. H1 R&D expense KRW 858,803M (11.7% of revenue).
quarterly_data.figure: Small-battery utilisation 73% (860 of 1,178 million cells); ASP KRW 2,923 per cell; H1 capex KRW 10,928 (100 million units); R&D KRW 858,803M

quarterly_data.signal: Customers: the report names BMW, Samsung Electronics, Stellantis and Volkswagen Group as main customers; five external customers each took 10% or more of H1 revenue (KRW 905,939M, 829,346M, 829,046M, 774,063M and 762,075M; names not disclosed). Related-party sales to Samsung Electronics and its subsidiaries were KRW 763,899,495 thousand in H1 2026 (H1 2025: KRW 678,157,303 thousand) and to Samsung Display KRW 166,923,192 thousand. 94% of Energy Solution sales go directly to customers, 6% via agents.
quarterly_data.figure: Five customers above 10%: KRW 905,939M / 829,346M / 829,046M / 774,063M / 762,075M; Samsung Electronics group KRW 763,899,495 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Suppliers, H1 2026 raw-material purchases (KRW 100 million units): electrode materials 23,725 (60%) from Umicore, EcoPro EM and others; assembly materials 8,555 (21%) from WCP, Sangsin EDP, Soulbrain and others; pack materials 7,444 (19%) from Powerlogics, Nexcon and others. Cathode active material averaged USD 24.79 per kg (FY2025: USD 27.05). Inventory purchases from the cathode JV EcoPro EM were KRW 835,125,556 thousand and from EcoPro BM KRW 49,424,142 thousand. On 03-24-2026 the company signed a mid- to long-term LFP cathode supply agreement with L&F.
quarterly_data.figure: Electrode materials 23,725 (60%), assembly 8,555 (21%), pack 7,444 (19%) in KRW 100 million; EcoPro EM purchases KRW 835,125,556 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Orders and contracts named in the report: an LFP battery supply contract for ESS with a large US energy company (12-10-2025); a prismatic ESS battery supply contract with a US energy company (03-16-2026); an EV battery supply contract with Mercedes-Benz (04-20-2026); a battery supply contract of subsidiary Samsung SDI America whose amount, counterparty and term are withheld for business confidentiality until 01-01-2030 (disclosed 01-30-2026); and a 2023 contract to supply next-generation P6 prismatic batteries from the Hungary plant for Hyundai Motor's next-generation European EVs for seven years from 2026. The company says it ships under basic supply agreements against customers' production plans, with volumes not fixed. Contract liabilities stood at KRW 733,267M (end-2025: KRW 721,753M).
quarterly_data.figure: Contract liabilities KRW 733,267M; Samsung SDI America contract terms withheld until 01-01-2030

quarterly_data.signal: Investment plans and targets (fair disclosures in the report): a KRW 9 trillion investment in a mother line to validate next-generation battery technology and advanced R&D in Cheonan (January 2026 to December 2040; disclosed 07-02-2026); a KRW 16 trillion investment in Ulsan to mass-produce next-generation all-solid-state batteries and LFP and sodium batteries for ESS as a global production base (January 2026 to December 2040; disclosed 07-03-2026) -- the company says both plans may change with market conditions. It targets all-solid-state battery mass production in 2027 and plans to develop and mass-produce sodium batteries. US capacity: the StarPlus Energy (Stellantis JV) plant 2 targets 34GWh a year with mass production in 2027; on 08-11-2026 the board decided to end the GM joint venture SDI-GM Synergy Cells and acquired GM's 49.99% stake, to run it as a sole subsidiary -- the New Carlisle, Indiana plant (about 27GWh, mass production targeted for 2027) is under construction and the original investment plan will change.
quarterly_data.figure: Cheonan KRW 9 trillion; Ulsan KRW 16 trillion (2026-2040); StarPlus plant 2 34GWh; GM JV plant about 27GWh; all-solid-state mass production target 2027
